correctness.rationale: The boundary in RESULT.md:9 is a union of punctured rays (t>0); none contains the origin. The Dirac measure at (0,0) is invariant and obeys the stated zero-mass condition, yet B_t=0 for all t instead of P(B_t=1)=1/n. The sector-weight step at lines 73–79 is where the missing mass enters. If the origin has mass eta, each of the q open sectors has mass (1-eta)/q and the process is a mixture of the stated cyclic process (weight 1-eta) and the all-zero sequence (weight eta). The ray-orbit and cyclic-overlap calculations themselves check out; excluding the origin would fix the scope, but does not resolve the contribution issues below. The finite support checks do not test the universal invariant-measure hypothesis.

originality.rationale: No source is credited with the false quantifier. The only natural corrected claim, the nonzero off-boundary law, is mechanically recoverable from the explicit induced dynamics in Lagarias–Rains Part I, Example 3.2: the negative branch is conjugate to rotation by theta=(n-1)pi/n in its half-plane; every exit into the other half-plane gives n positive steps with action -I. At negative return times, reducing the angle modulo pi therefore gives theta mod pi=-pi/n. Exactly one of the n negative returns does not exit the half-plane (the stay interval has width pi-theta=pi/n); the gaps in the sign word are one gap of 1 and n-1 gaps of n+1. This determines the entire cyclic sign word up to shift, not just its frequency. Stationarity takes the uniform cyclic shifts of that word, and interval overlaps give the displayed two-time classification. The statistics were not found stated verbatim, but their absence from the sources inspected is not evidence of new dynamical content.
residual_risks: Earlier exact wording in Beardon–Bullett–Rippon was not verifiable from the primary text; the mathematical implication used in the decision is already present in the accessible Lagarias–Rains example.
